   PROPERTY MAINTENANCE AND
  BUILDING REHABILITATION APPEALS BOARD
  SPECIAL MEETING
  JUNE 22, 2022

Chair Apodaca called the special hybrid meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. in the Norwalk City
Hall, Council Chambers and via video/teleconference pursuant to the provisions of
Assembly Bill 361. Responding to roll call were Chair Apodaca in person, and Board
Members Barragan, Garcia, and Navas, via video/teleconference. Vice Chair Lopez was
absent. Also present were Gabriela Garcia, Management Analyst; Beth Chow, Senior
Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann, Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES
The Board approved the minutes of the Regular Meeting of June 16, 2021.

REPORT OF DELINQUENT TRASH ACCOUNTS

Chair Apodaca opened the public hearing.

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Gabriela Garcia, Management
Analyst, presented a report stating that the City of Norwalk provides mandatory refuse
service to protect the public health and welfare of its residents; that, as such, Athens
Services picks up trash weekly billing customers on a quarterly basis; that payment for
services is due within thirty (30) days from the billing date; that a late fee of $25.00 is
added if payment has not been made by the end of the service quarter; that the hauler
makes attempts during the year to collect on past-due accounts; that as authorized in the
Municipal Code, the hauler is allowed to seek payment through the tax rolls in July of
each year for the period of May 1st of the previous year through April 30th of the current
year; that in May of this year, 2,710 notices were prepared and mailed to all property
owners with a delinquent balance as of April 30, 2022; that the delinquent amounts totaled
$337,903; that since the notices went out, some delinquent accounts have been paid and
payments will continue to be received until July 31st; and that staff recommends that the
Board forward the delinquent properties to City Council with a recommendation that the
delinquent properties be placed on the County Tax Roll unless the outstanding balance
is paid by July 31st.

As there were no persons wishing to speak on this item, Chair Apodaca closed the public
hearing.

Board Member Garcia stated that he would like a follow-up update on the success of
collection efforts at a six-month and a one-year interval. In response to Board Member
Garcia’s comment, Senior Planner Chow indicated that staff is going to provide an email
to the Board Members in December of this year with the information requested.

It was moved by Chair Apodaca and seconded by Board Member Navas to forward the
listed properties to the City Council with a recommendation that the delinquent properties

AUTHORITY:

Norwalk Municipal Code Section 8.48.280, Mandatory Service, requires all solid waste
collected from a residential or commercial/industrial premise for a fee, service charge, or
other consideration, shall be collected by a solid waste enterprise under the provisions of
an exclusive contract awarded by the City Council.

BACKGROUND:

City procedures state that any owner who has a delinquent account as of May 1, 2023
which covers the period of May 1, 2022 to April 30, 2023 shall be sent, by mail, written
notification that the Appeals Board will review all such delinquent accounts during a public
hearing. On May 1, 2023, Athens Services, the City’s solid waste hauler, mailed 2,827
notices that sought a combined amount of $421,850. As of June 1, 2023, there are 1,821
accounts that have not paid off their balance.

Daily payments and/or adjustments are being processed and will continue through July
31, 2023. A City administrative fee of $25 will be added to each delinquent account not
paid by July 31, 2023.

FISCAL IMPACT:

The City will be reimbursed $25 for each account on the final lien list for administrative
costs. The total amount will not be known until the final list is complete on July 31, 2023.

AUTHORITY

Section 15.32.150.E of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) authorizes the Building
Rehabilitation Appeals Board to hold hearings related to work completed on private properties
to eliminate a hazard or to remove an unsafe condition or take any action that would result in a
cost assessment against the property.

Section 15.32.150.A of the NMC declares buildings public nuisances, if they are found
“structurally unsafe or not provided with adequate egress, or which constitute a fire hazard, or
are otherwise dangerous to human life, or which in relation to existing use constitute a hazard
to safety or health or public welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation,
obsolescence, fire hazard, disaster damage, or abandonment, as specified in this Code or in
any other effective ordinance or statute.” Further such buildings shall be abated by repair,
rehabilitation, improvement, removal, or demolition, in whole or part, in accordance with the
procedures specified in the NMC.

Section 15.32.170 of the NMC authorizes the Building Official to serve as the record owner and
person having control of buildings that are deemed unsafe and pose a safety hazard to the
adjacent community, and accords the Building Official authority to prevent unauthorized persons
from gaining access to such structures.

Section 15.32.170.12 of the NMC establishes emergency procedures for the Building Official to
remedy immediate hazards to unsafe buildings or structures by limiting access to such buildings

BACKGROUND:

Staff takes emergency action to secure or otherwise abate the hazardous conditions to protect
the public whenever unsafe conditions are found to create a hazard to safety, health or public
welfare, by reason of inadequate maintenance, dilapidation, fire hazard, disaster damage,
vandalism or abandonment.

When the City steps in to secure properties and incurs a cost, the property owner on record is
sent an invoice for such work. Unpaid invoices are processed as a special assessment to the
property. Further, a “Declaration of Substandard” is filed with the Los Angeles County
Recorder’s Office as part of the nuisance abatement process to notify interested parties of the
pending cost associated with the abatement.

The purpose of the meeting tonight is to provide the opportunity for any interested party to voice
their concerns or objections to such assessments before the Board.

DISCUSSION:

Notice of the abatement expenses are sent as an invoice to the property owners of record. Staff
keeps an account of the abatement expenses and maintains the list of unpaid invoices as an
itemized written report to the Property Maintenance and Building Rehabilitation Appeals Board
for confirmation (Attachment No. 1). Property owners liable to assessment may bring objections
of such assessments before the Board.

The Board shall hear all objections or protests of property owners liable to be assessed for the
delinquent fees, and may make revisions to the report and recommendations to the City Council
with regard to disposition of the delinquent fees.

Upon the recommendation of the Board and confirmation by the City Council, the cost of
abatement will constitute a lien on the property and may be paid to the Director of Finance prior
to August 1, 2023. The unpaid liens will be delivered to the County Auditor to be collected at
the time and in the manner of other taxes on the property.

Attachment No. 1 details the properties that were invoiced for emergency board-up performed
pursuant to Chapter 15.32 of the Norwalk Municipal Code for which reimbursement has not been
